newsitem.title: INDIA: India 97/98 sugar output to dip sharply - trade.
newsitem.headline: India 97/98 sugar output to dip sharply - trade.

text.p: India's sugar output in the 1997/98 (October-September) season is expected to dip sharply to 10.5 million tonnes from 12.8 million in 1996/97, the Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) said on Friday.
"We expect sugar output of 10.5 million tonnes in the next season," M. Manickam, president of ISMA, told Reuters.
"We expect a lot of crop diversion because farmers got better prices in this season in crops such as wheat," said Manickam.
He said India would start the 1997/98 season with a carryover stock of 6.6 million tonnes.
"This stock plus the output will see India comfortable in the next season. But in 1998/99 we will have a problem," he added.
Manickam expected the domestic demand for sugar in 1997/98 to be about 15 million tonnes. He did not give comparative figures for the previous year.
